After being elected, in the months prior to his inauguration, García sought to heal Peru's relationship with [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile "Chile"), strained by the differences between the governments of [Alejandro Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alejandro_Toledo "Alejandro Toledo") and [Ricardo Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Lagos "Ricardo Lagos") and severely impaired by former President [Alberto Fujimori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Fujimori "Alberto Fujimori")'s extradition affair.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-70) García's intentions were well received by [Michelle Bachelet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Bachelet "Michelle Bachelet"), President of Chile, as she and García met and struck some preliminary agreements.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-71)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-72) These conversations eventually led to the final draft of a landmark economic agreement with Chile a month after García was sworn in.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-73)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-74)

On 9 November 2006, three months after being inaugurated, García signed 12 commercial agreements with President [Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_In%C3%A1cio_Lula_da_Silva "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva") of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"),[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-75)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-76) strengthening the relationship between the two countries. As part of the [IIRSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IIRSA "IIRSA") programme and continuing integration efforts – including the August 2006 negotiations between [Petrobras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petrobras "Petrobras") and [Petroperú](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroper%C3%BA "Petroperú")[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-77) – these new agreements sought to further bilateral cooperation.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-78) García offered Peruvian [hydropower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydropower "Hydropower") to meet Brazil's growing energy needs, although further details were not disclosed.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-79)

## Post-presidency (2011–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alan_Garc%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Post-presidency (2011–2019)")]

García, as he offered during the 2011 electoral campaign, made himself available to the new Head of State to serve the interests of Peru in the manner required.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-80)

In addition, he also dedicated himself to writing opinion articles, mainly on his internal and external vision, primarily aimed at reducing poverty in Peru, increasing foreign investment and issues related to the growth of the Peruvian economy with social sensitivity.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-81)

The salary increase for ministers carried out in February 2014 was harshly criticized by the former president, who during his government cut the salary of his Cabinet members by half, which, according to official spokesmen, caused a talent drain of the state apparatus. Through his Twitter account, he described the measure as "the great deal."

García ran for a third term as president in the [2016 Peruvian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Peruvian_general_election "2016 Peruvian general election") as the candidate of the criticized [Popular Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_Alliance_(Peru) "Popular Alliance (Peru)") coalition which included APRA's old rival, the [Christian People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_People's_Party_(Peru) "Christian People's Party (Peru)") with [Lourdes Flores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lourdes_Flores "Lourdes Flores") as his first running mate. The election's first round polls gave García 5.83% of the popular vote, preventing him from participating in the [runoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runoff_(election) "Runoff (election)") election.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-82)[Pedro Pablo Kuczynski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Pablo_Kuczynski "Pedro Pablo Kuczynski") was ultimately elected.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-83)

### Mega-commission

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alan_Garc%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Mega-commission")]

In 2013, a mega-commission was formed which lasted five years to investigate the alleged irregularities of the second government of Alan García, with the nationalist Sergio Tejada as head. Of the eight cases that the mega-commission analyzed, in none of them was the commission able to continue the investigations against the former president because he presented an [amparo action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recurso_de_amparo "Recurso de amparo") against the commission, alleging the violation of due process. Consequently, the judiciary annulled everything that had been done with regard to García, thus preventing the investigation from continuing.

García in 2010 with Brazilian president [Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_In%C3%A1cio_Lula_da_Silva "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva")

The Peruvian press reported that in May 2012, after leaving office, García was paid US$100,000 to give a speech to Brazilian business leaders in São Paulo, money which was later characterized in the media as, and suspected by Peruvian prosecutors to be, a [kickback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kickback_(bribery) "Kickback (bribery)") from the [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil") construction company [Odebrecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odebrecht "Odebrecht"). Because García reported and paid taxes on each payment he received, and multiple organizations were willing to pay him to have him as speaker, his defense and lawyers were optimistic that they could show that the payments did not constitute bribery.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-84)

In 2016 and 2017, five of García's former ministers were accused of [corruption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corruption "Corruption") by the Peruvian justice system: [Yehude Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yehude_Simon "Yehude Simon") (Prime Minister), [Rosario Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosario_Fern%C3%A1ndez "Rosario Fernández") (Minister of Justice), [Mercedes Cabanillas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes_Cabanillas "Mercedes Cabanillas") (Minister of the Interior), [Ántero Flores Aráoz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81ntero_Flores_Ar%C3%A1oz "Ántero Flores Aráoz") (Minister of Defence), and [Luis Nava Guibert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Nava_Guibert "Luis Nava Guibert") (Minister of Production).[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-85)

In November 2018, García was banned from leaving Peru by the courts due to the Odebrecht scandal investigation. He entered the residence of the Uruguayan ambassador on 17 November, requesting [asylum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asylum_seeker "Asylum seeker"). Thus, on 18 November, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Peru reported that the ambassador of the Eastern Republic of Uruguay had communicated the entry of the former president to his residence and the request for diplomatic asylum.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-86) The Minister of Relations Uruguayan Foreign Ministry, [Rodolfo Nin Novoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodolfo_Nin_Novoa "Rodolfo Nin Novoa"), reported that Uruguay had decided to process the asylum application. On 20 November, the Peruvian Foreign Ministry delivered a diplomatic note to the Uruguayan ambassador, Carlos Barros, on the request for diplomatic asylum presented by Alan García, expressing the position of the Peruvian government and denying the existence of political persecution.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-87) However, on 3 December his request was denied, and he subsequently left the ambassador's residence.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-88) On January 4, 2019, García appeared before the prosecutor's office as a witness to testify in the investigation carried out against Miguel Atala (former vice president of PetroPerú), for having received a bribe from the [Odebrecht company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novonor "Novonor").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-89)

The scandal also led to arrests, [where possible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extradition_request "Extradition request"), of all of the other [living former presidents of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Peru#Living_former_presidents_of_Peru "President of Peru") who had served since 2000: [Pedro Pablo Kuczynski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Pablo_Kuczynski "Pedro Pablo Kuczynski"), [Ollanta Humala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ollanta_Humala "Ollanta Humala"), and [Alejandro Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alejandro_Toledo "Alejandro Toledo").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-90)

## Suicide

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alan_Garc%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Suicide")]

On 17 April 2019, García shot himself in the head while hiding in his bedroom as he was being presented with a ten-day preliminary arrest warrant related to investigations for corruption and bribes his presidential secretary allegedly received from Odebrecht.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-timeline-91) Initial reports stated that officers had violated protocol, allowing García to be alone with the excuse that he was going to talk with his lawyer.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-:0-14)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-timeline-91) He was taken to the Casimiro Ulloa hospital and underwent an emergency surgical procedure, during which he experienced three [cardiac arrests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_arrest "Cardiac arrest").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-:0-14)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-92) After four hours, his death was announced by the heads of the [American Popular Revolutionary Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Popular_Revolutionary_Alliance "American Popular Revolutionary Alliance") (APRA) political party and Nidia Vílchez, with the cause being a "massive" [cerebral hemorrhage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_hemorrhage "Cerebral hemorrhage") and cardiorespiratory arrest.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-timeline-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-93)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-:0-14)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-94) According to police sources, García had shot himself with his [Colt Anaconda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colt_Anaconda "Colt Anaconda") revolver, which had been given to him as a gift by the [Peruvian Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Navy "Peruvian Navy") during his second term, and was among nine other firearms that the former president was licensed to own.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-95)

A few hours after his death was announced, García's body was taken in a wooden casket to the APRA headquarters in Lima, where a memorial service was held on the same day.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-memorial-96) President [Martín Vizcarra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mart%C3%ADn_Vizcarra "Martín Vizcarra") declared a three-day mourning period.

Various Peruvian and foreign authorities and personalities expressed their condolences to the family for the death of the former president.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-97) On social media and on the Peruvian diaspora, public opinion was more polarized.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-98)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-99)

## Public image

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alan_Garc%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Public image")]

García was 2008 _[Latin Business Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin\_Business\_Chronicle "Latin Business Chronicle")_'s "leader of the year" at a time when Peru was ranked as Latin America's third-best country for business.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-100)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-101)

However, corruption scandals during his second presidency have led 35% of Peruvians to consider Garcia's administration the most corrupt in the country's history. This is according to a 2017 survey by [Ipsos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipsos "Ipsos") of 1314 people, commissioned by Proética, the Peruvian chapter of [Transparency International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transparency_International "Transparency International"). The survey found that, in terms of levels of corruption, Garcia's administration is followed by that of his first successor, Fujimori (23%), and that of his second successor, Humala, in third place (22%).[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-102) Garcia himself has been rated as one of the most corrupt Peruvian politicians, when not the most, in surveys done after his second term ended, in the mid-to-late 2010s, by Proética, Datum, [Perú 21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per%C3%BA_21 "Perú 21") and Gestión magazine.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-103)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-104)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa#cite_note-105)

The **National University of San Marcos** (Spanish: _Universidad Nacional Mayor de San Marcos_, **UNMSM**) is a [public](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_university "Public university")[research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") located in [Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima "Lima"), the capital of [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru"). In the Americas, it is the first officially established ([privilege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privilege_(legal_ethics) "Privilege (legal ethics)") by [Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_V,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor")) and the [oldest continuously operating university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_oldest_universities_in_continuous_operation#Latin_America_and_the_Caribbean "List of oldest universities in continuous operation").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-dean-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Fundaci%C3%B3n_de_la_Universidad_de_Santo_Domingo-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-The_Founding_of_Harvard_College._Appendix_A:_The_Student_Universities_of_Bologna,_Spain,_and_Spanish_America-11)

The university started in the general studies that were offered in the convent of the Rosario of the order of Santo Domingo—the current [Basilica and Convent of Santo Domingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_and_Convent_of_Santo_Domingo,_Lima "Basilica and Convent of Santo Domingo, Lima")—on July 1, 1548.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-ADL2024-12) Its official foundation was conceived by [Fray Thomas de San Martín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fray_Thomas_de_San_Mart%C3%ADn "Fray Thomas de San Martín") on May 12, 1551; with the decree of Emperor [Charles I of Spain and V of the Holy Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_V,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor"). In 1571, it acquired the degree of pontifical granted by [Pope Pius V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Pius_V "Pope Pius V"), with which it ended up being named the "Royal and Pontifical University of the City of the Kings of Lima".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Cedvla_real_del_se%C3%B1or_emperador_Carlos_V,_y_la_reyna_do%C3%B1a_Juana_su_madre,_sobre_la_fundaci%C3%B3n_de_ella_Real_Vniversidad-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Fundaci%C3%B3n_de_la_Universidad_de_Lima-14) It is also referred to as the "University of Lima" throughout the [Viceroyalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_Peru "Viceroyalty of Peru").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_II:_Conquista_y_Virreinato-15)

The University of San Marcos has passed through several locations, of which it maintains and stands out: the "[Casona de San Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casona_of_the_National_University_of_San_Marcos "Casona of the National University of San Marcos")", one of the buildings in the [Historic Center of Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historic_Centre_of_Lima "Historic Centre of Lima") that were recognized as [World Heritage Sites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") by [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO") in 1988.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Historic_Centre_of_Lima-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Historic_Centre_of_Lima:_Gallery-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Casona_de_San_Marcos:_remanso_cultural_en_el_Centro_de_Lima-18) The University of San Marcos has 66 professional schools,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-19) grouped into 20 faculties,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Facultades-20) and these in turn in 5 academic areas.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-%C3%81reas_acad%C3%A9micas_de_la_Universidad_Nacional_Mayor_de_San_Marcos-21) Through its "Domingo Angulo" historical archive, the university preserves documents and writings. In 2019, the "Colonial Fund and Foundational Documents of the National University of San Marcos: 1551–1852" was incorporated into the [UNESCO Memory of the World Register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_of_the_World_Programme "Memory of the World Programme").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Documentos_hist%C3%B3ricos_de_San_Marcos_son_reconocidos_como_patrimonio_mundial_por_la_Unesco-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Documentos_hist%C3%B3ricos_de_la_UNMSM_son_reconocidos_como_Patrimonio_Mundial_por_la_Unesco-23)

It holds a ten-year institutional licensing granted by the National Superintendency of Higher Education (SUNEDU) and an international institutional accreditation.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-24) To date, twenty-one Presidents of the Republic of Peru,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-25) seven Peruvian candidates for the Nobel Prizes in Physics, Literature, and Peace,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-26) and the only Peruvian Nobel Prize laureate[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-29) have been alumni or professors of this institution.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 10: Óleo referente a la fundación de la Universidad de San Marcos, oficialmente la primera universidad del Perú y de América, y a su gestor fray Tomás de San Martín.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Unmsm_fundacion1551.jpg/250px-Unmsm_fundacion1551.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Unmsm_fundacion1551.jpg)

Oil referring to the founding of the University of San Marcos

### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early history")]

During the General Studies carried out in the cloisters of the Convent of the Rosario of the Order of Santo Domingo—current [Basilica and Convento de Santo Domingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_and_Convent_of_Santo_Domingo,_Lima "Basilica and Convent of Santo Domingo, Lima")—on July 1, 1548,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-ADL2024-12) the [Cabildo of Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabildo_of_Lima "Cabildo of Lima") would send [Fray Tomás de San Martín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fray_Thomas_de_San_Mart%C3%ADn "Fray Thomas de San Martín") and Captain Juan Jerónimo de Aliaga to Spain, who obtained the [founding order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_c%C3%A9dula "Real cédula") of the university from [Charles I of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_V,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor") and [V of the Holy Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_V,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor") and [Queen Juana I of Castile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_of_Castile "Joanna of Castile"). The foundation of the Royal University of the City of Kings was officially carried out.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-UNMSM:_Historia-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Antecedentes_hist%C3%B3ricos_de_la_UNMSM-31) The university began to function officially on January 2, 1553.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-La_universidad_no_es_una_isla:_Un_pr%C3%B3logo,_un_estudio,_un_plan,_y_tres_discursos-32)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/UNMSM_SalaCapitular_ConventodeSantoDomingo.jpg/250px-UNMSM_SalaCapitular_ConventodeSantoDomingo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UNMSM_SalaCapitular_ConventodeSantoDomingo.jpg)

The chapter house in the Convent of the Rosario of the Dominicans

They asked the Royal Court for compliance with the [Royal decree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_decree "Royal decree") of 1570. The university moved to its second location, near the outskirts of San Marcelo, where the Convent of the [Order of Saint Augustine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Saint_Augustine "Order of Saint Augustine") had previously operated.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-UNMSM:_Historia-30) The "Royal and Pontifical University of San Marcos" was chosen as its official name on September 6, 1574, with [Mark the Evangelist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_the_Evangelist "Mark the Evangelist") as the patron saint of the University.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Antecedentes_hist%C3%B3ricos_de_la_UNMSM-31) In 1575, the university changed its location again to [the old Plaza del Estanque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legislative_Palace_(Peru) "Legislative Palace (Peru)").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Fundaci%C3%B3n_de_la_Universidad_de_Lima-14)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-La_universidad_no_es_una_isla:_Un_pr%C3%B3logo,_un_estudio,_un_plan,_y_tres_discursos-32)

The officially named University of San Marcos began its work in the viceregal era with the faculties of [Theology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faculty_of_Pontifical_and_Civil_Theology_of_Lima "Faculty of Pontifical and Civil Theology of Lima") and Arts,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XIV:_Literatura-33) later the canons of Law and Medicine would be created. On November 27, 1579, the professors asked [King Philip II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_II_of_Spain "Philip II of Spain") for the institution of jurisdiction that governed the [University of Salamanca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Salamanca "University of Salamanca"). In 1581, Viceroy Francisco Álvarez de Toledo authorized clerics and laymen to be elected.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-UNMSM:_Historia,_Continuidad_universitaria-34)

### 1700s to 1900s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1700s to 1900s")]

The support for the secularization of the University of San Marcos was given by [Viceroy Francisco Álvarez de Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_de_Toledo "Francisco de Toledo"). It was also exercised by the rector of the [Royal Convictory of San Carlos](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real%20Convictorio%20de%20San%20Carlos "es:Real Convictorio de San Carlos").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_II:_Conquista_y_Virreinato-15) Between 1792 and 1811, the amphitheater and medicine chairs began to develop in the Royal Hospital of San Andrés. Both the University of San Marcos and the College of Law and Letters of San Carlos and the [College of Medicine of San Fernando](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facultad%20de%20Medicina%20%C2%ABSan%20Fernando%C2%BB%20(Universidad%20Nacional%20Mayor%20de%20San%20Marcos) "es:Facultad de Medicina «San Fernando» (Universidad Nacional Mayor de San Marcos)") began to be watched by the Viceroy because their house professors and students were suspected of envisioning.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Rese%C3%B1a_hist%C3%B3rica_de_la_Universidad_Nacional_Mayor_de_San_Marcos-35)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Primer_Congreso_Constituyente_del_Per%C3%BA_%281822%29_-_Capilla_de_la_Universidad_San_Marcos.jpg/250px-Primer_Congreso_Constituyente_del_Per%C3%BA_%281822%29_-_Capilla_de_la_Universidad_San_Marcos.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Primer_Congreso_Constituyente_del_Per%C3%BA_(1822)_-_Capilla_de_la_Universidad_San_Marcos.jpg)

The First Constituent Congress of Peru was chaired by [Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toribio_Rodr%C3%ADguez_de_Mendoza "Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza") on September 20, 1822.

The University of San Marcos became part of the current [Republic of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru") since its independence in 1821. The [First Constituent Congress of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituent_Congress_of_Peru,_1822 "Constituent Congress of Peru, 1822") was initially chaired by the former rector of the University of San Marcos, [Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toribio_Rodr%C3%ADguez_de_Mendoza "Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza"); of the 64 constituent deputies, 54 were San Marcos's alumnus and Carolines's.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Antecedentes_hist%C3%B3ricos_de_la_UNMSM-31)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Rese%C3%B1a_hist%C3%B3rica_del_Congreso-36) In 1822, the university handed over its collection of 50,000 books to form the National Library of Peru. In 1840, the Colleges of San Carlos and San Fernando are taken over by the University of San Marcos. San Marcos was empowered by the then President [Ramón Castilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_Castilla "Ramón Castilla") to approve new universities and control the newly created ones.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Rese%C3%B1a_hist%C3%B3rica_de_la_Universidad_Nacional_Mayor_de_San_Marcos-35)

During the 1870s, the university moved to the [Casona of San Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casona_of_the_National_University_of_San_Marcos "Casona of the National University of San Marcos"). During the [War of the Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_Pacific "War of the Pacific") and specifically during the [occupation of Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupation_of_Lima "Occupation of Lima") by [Chilean troops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilean_Army "Chilean Army"), art and cultural objects and assets were taken from the university in order to be taken to Chile by sea.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Antecedentes_hist%C3%B3ricos_de_la_UNMSM-31) At the end of the 19th century, the San Fernando Faculty of Medicine, which was located in a building in the old Plaza de Santa Ana, moved to its current location in the Orchard of Mestas.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XII:_Salud-37) Once the war ended, by law of 1901, it is stated that Peruvian university education corresponds to the National University of San Marcos and the minor universities of [Trujillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_Trujillo "National University of Trujillo"), Cusco, and Arequipa, which were later joined by the [Catholic University of Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_Catholic_University_of_Peru "Pontifical Catholic University of Peru") and technical schools.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Rese%C3%B1a_hist%C3%B3rica_de_la_Universidad_Nacional_Mayor_de_San_Marcos-35)

### Modern history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Modern history")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/UniversidaddeSanMarco_AugustoBLeguia.jpg/250px-UniversidaddeSanMarco_AugustoBLeguia.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UniversidaddeSanMarco_AugustoBLeguia.jpg)

Then President Augusto Leguía after a speech at the university

At the beginning of the 20th century, university activists promoted a reform within the University of San Marcos.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-La_universidad_no_es_una_isla:_Un_pr%C3%B3logo,_un_estudio,_un_plan,_y_tres_discursos-32) In 1909, the students had participated in protests against the [Peruvian dictatorial governments](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rep%C3%BAblica%20Aristocr%C3%A1tica "es:República Aristocrática"). In 1916, the Federation of Students of Peru (FEP) was established, led mainly by students from San Marcos. The FEP's demands included university reforms such as updating curricula, removing untrained faculty, and eliminating Peruvian government interference in the university. The university educational system was later reorganized and university autonomy was granted.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Lima:_A_cultural_history:_The_Casona_de_San_Marcos-38)

In 1946, the university's name was made official as the Universidad Nacional Mayor de San Marcos. In 1951, as a commemoration of the 400th anniversary of the founding of the University of San Marcos, the university acquires a new piece of land to build the new [University City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_City_of_the_National_University_of_San_Marcos "University City of the National University of San Marcos"), where the [Stadium of the University of San Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Universidad_San_Marcos "Estadio Universidad San Marcos") was inaugurated that same year. A ceremony was also held that brought together the rectors of the main Ibero-American universities, who decided to give her the title of "Dean of America". Due to this, the university has retained the names of the **University of Peru** and the **Dean of the Americas**.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-San_Marcos_al_d%C3%ADa_(n%C2%B0_212):_San_Marcos_en_la_sociedad_del_conocimiento-7)

In 1958, then Vice President [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") had scheduled a conference at the University of San Marcos as part of his visit to Latin America; however, this did not take place due to the protest of San Marcos, who spoke out against US policy in the region with phrases such as "Nixon, Go Home!".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Huellas_digitales:_la_accidentada_visita_de_Richard_Nixon_al_Per%C3%BA-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-El_centenario_de_Mr._Nixon-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Nixon_en_San_Marcos:_Im%C3%A1genes_in%C3%A9ditas-41) The conference was transferred to the [Catholic University of Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_Catholic_University_of_Peru "Pontifical Catholic University of Peru").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-The_Harvard_Crimson_(May_12,_1958):_Nixon_in_Peru-42)

In the mid-1960s, several faculties of the university began to move to the Ciudad Universitaria site, where 17 of the 20 faculties are currently located.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-San_Marcos_al_d%C3%ADa_(n%C2%B0_126):_456:_1551_-_12_de_mayo_-_2007-43) On September 22, 1984, the current statute of the university was promulgated. It had nearly 40,000 students and more than 4,000 faculty.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-San_Marcos_al_d%C3%ADa_(n%C2%B0_165):_San_Marcos,_luz_de_la_inteligencia_del_Per%C3%BA_y_Am%C3%A9rica-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XI:_Ciencia_y_Tecnolog%C3%ADa-45) In 2010, a [Nobel Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize") was awarded to [Mario Vargas Llosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Vargas_Llosa "Mario Vargas Llosa"), a student of the University of San Marcos.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-The_Nobel_Prize_in_Literature_2010:_Mario_Vargas_Llosa-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Peruvian_wins_Nobel_for_literature-47) As a tribute, on March 30, 2011, the university distinguished Vargas Llosa with its highest decoration: the San Marcos Medal of Honor in the degree of [Grand Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Cross "Grand Cross"). The ceremony was held in the Casona de San Marcos.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Primera_universidad-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-UNMSM_distinguir%C3%A1_a_Vargas_Llosa_con_m%C3%A1xima_condecoraci%C3%B3n-49) In 2019, the university awards a doctoral degree based on a thesis written and defended entirely in Quechua.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Roxana_Quispe_Collantes:_Tesis_imperial-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-UNMSM_Oct_16,_2019-51)

### University symbols

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: University symbols")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Cedula_Real_1551_Universidad_de_San_Marcos.png/250px-Cedula_Real_1551_Universidad_de_San_Marcos.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cedula_Real_1551_Universidad_de_San_Marcos.png)

Royal Decree in which Emperor Charles V authorized the creation of the National University of San Marcos

Since its foundation until 1574, the first official shield showed an image of the [Virgen del Rosario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_of_the_Rosary "Virgin of the Rosary"), considered the patron saint of the Dominican friars; on the right, a representation of the [Pacific Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean"); and below a lime—fruit, referring to the city of Lima. The coat of arms was approved by King Charles I of Spain in 1551. By the end of 1570, after the papal bull of [Pius V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Pius_V "Pope Pius V"), the coat of arms was modified, replacing the image of the Virgen del Rosario with that of the new patron of the university, the apostle [Saint Mark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_the_Evangelist "Mark the Evangelist") and the [Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lion_of_Saint_Mark "Lion of Saint Mark"). For the coat of arms, the documents about them in the century were black and white. It was not until 1929 that the colors, blue for the 'ocean', black or brown for the image of the saint, light blue for the background, and silver for the columns, became used. The second original shield with the image of San Marcos has been the longest-lasting symbol of the university. In 1929, the original colors were officially introduced: blue for the 'ocean', black or brown for the image of the saint, light blue for the background, and silver for the columns.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Escudo_de_San_Marcos-52)

The University of San Marcos was originally governed by clerics of monastic orders; during the [Age of Enlightenment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment "Age of Enlightenment"), the [Bourbon Reforms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourbon_Reforms "Bourbon Reforms") transformed it into a secular institution. The University Assembly is the highest governing body in the university.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-%C3%93rganos_de_gobierno:_Asamblea_Universitaria-56) It is made up of the rector and the two vice-rectors, the deans of the faculties, the director of the graduate school, representatives of the teachers, and representatives of the students—which constitute a third of the total number of members of the assembly—representatives of the graduates, and the president of the Federation of students of the University of San Marcos with the right to speak, without a vote.

Administrative officials of the highest level can attend the assembly when they are required as advisors, without the right to vote.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-%C3%93rganos_de_gobierno:_Asamblea_Universitaria-56) The main attributions of the university assembly are: the modification of the statute of the university, requiring in such a case the majority of its members; approval of the General Plan for the operation of the university and carrying out its evaluation; it is in charge of the election of the rector and vice-rectors.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-%C3%93rganos_de_gobierno:_Asamblea_Universitaria-56)

The University Council is the body in charge of the direction and execution of the university.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-%C3%93rganos_de_gobierno:_Consejo_Universitario-57) The representative of the graduates and the president of the Federation of Students have the right to speak, without a vote. Administrative officials of the highest level can attend the council when they are required as advisers, without the right to vote.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-%C3%93rganos_de_gobierno:_Consejo_Universitario-57) The powers of the council are: to formulate the general plan for the development and operation of the university, as well as to establish its policies.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-%C3%93rganos_de_gobierno:_Consejo_Universitario-57)

The Rectorate is the university's governing body, consisting mainly of the Rector. The rector is the first executive authority of the university, as well as its legal representative and its institutional image. The University of San Marcos has had 216 rectors since its foundation.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Autoridades:_Galer%C3%ADa_de_Rectores_de_la_UNMSM-55) Its Vice-Rectorate is made up of two vice-rectors: one for undergraduate academics and the other for research and postgraduate.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Vicerrectorado_Acad%C3%A9mico_de_la_UNMSM-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Vicerrectorado_de_Investigaci%C3%B3n_de_la_UNMSM-59) The government and administration of the faculties and schools are in charge of the Deans and the School Directors, respectively.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Autoridades:_Decanos-60) In addition, the postgraduate units of each faculty are in charge of their respective directors, with the Director of the Graduate School as the general director.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Autoridades:_Director_de_la_Escuela_de_Postgrado-61)

### Faculties and academic structure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Faculties and academic structure")]

The University of San Marcos has 20 faculties grouped into 5 academic areas, in which 65 undergraduate programs, 77 master's degrees, and 27 doctorates are offered.

#### Health Sciences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Health Sciences")]

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/UNMSM_Facultad_de_Medicina_San_Fernando.jpg/250px-UNMSM_Facultad_de_Medicina_San_Fernando.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UNMSM_Facultad_de_Medicina_San_Fernando.jpg)

Interior of the main building of the campus of the Faculty of Medicine "San Fernando"

Faculty of Medicine San Fernando is the Faculty of Human Medicine of the University of San Marcos. It is also called the "San Fernando" Faculty of Medicine. After the creation of the Royal College of Medicine and Surgery of San Fernando in 1811, it was installed as faculty on October 6, 1856, by [Cayetano Heredia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cayetano_Heredia "Cayetano Heredia").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XII:_Salud7-62) In the National Medical Exams in Peru, the "San Fernando" Faculty of Medicine has obtained first place on numerous occasions.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Resultados_del_Examen_Nacional_de_Medicina_(ENAM)_20082-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Resultados_del_Examen_Nacional_de_Medicina_(ENAM)_20092-64)

The Faculty of Pharmacy and Biochemistry was started in 1931. It would not be until October 29, 1943, that the law approved the creation of the Faculty of Pharmacy and Biochemistry.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XII:_Salud7-62) The faculty offers studies of undergraduate, specialization, and postgraduate.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Facultad_de_Farmacia_y_Bioqu%C3%ADmica2-65) The Faculty of Dentistry was created in 1920. In the following year, this institute was incorporated.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XII:_Salud7-62) It has dental clinics.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Facultad_de_Odontolog%C3%ADa-66)

The National School of Agronomy and the [Chorrillos Military School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chorrillos_Military_School "Chorrillos Military School") would come together, creating the National School of Veterinary Sciences, which in 1946 would become the current Faculty of Veterinary Medicine.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XII:_Salud7-62) In 1956, the faculty moved to its current location in [San Borja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Borja_District "San Borja District").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Facultad_de_Medicina_Veterinaria-67) The Faculty of Psychology was created in 1963.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XII:_Salud7-62)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Facultad_de_Psicolog%C3%ADa2-68)

Main pavilion of the Faculty of Mathematical Sciences

The Faculty of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering was created on April 7, 1855. The faculty was started by Antonio Raimondi and José Eboli. In 1946, then President [José Luis Bustamante y Rivero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Luis_Bustamante_y_Rivero "José Luis Bustamante y Rivero") promulgated Law 10555, which created the Faculty of Chemistry at the University of San Marcos. On April 24, 1964, the study of chemical engineering was introduced, with which the faculty acquired the current name of Faculty of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XI:_Ciencia_y_Tecnolog%C3%ADa3-69)

The Faculty of Biological Sciences became independent on March 15, 1866. In the 20th century, there was a reform of the biological sciences study program and the granting of the professional title of biologist was established.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XI:_Ciencia_y_Tecnolog%C3%ADa3-69) The Faculty of Physical Sciences was officially instituted in 1966.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XI:_Ciencia_y_Tecnolog%C3%ADa3-69) The Faculty of Mathematical Sciences began its operation in the year 1850. In 1862, it was called the Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics; in 1876, it was named the Faculty of Sciences. It is located in Ciudad Universitaria.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Escuela_acad%C3%A9mico-profesional_de_Computaci%C3%B3n_Cient%C3%ADfica-70)

In 2009 and 2014, the School of Civil Engineering and the School of Environmental Engineering were created respectively; this being the final conformation of the current Faculty of Geological, Mining, Metallurgical and Geographic Engineering.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_XI:_Ciencia_y_Tecnolog%C3%ADa3-69)

The Faculty of Industrial Engineering was established in 1969. The Faculty of Letters and Human Sciences started from the faculties of theology and arts, which would later derive the Faculty of Letters. In 1854, under the government of [Ramón Castilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_Castilla "Ramón Castilla"), it adopted the name of Faculty of Philosophy and Humanities. It is located mainly in the University City; it also has the San Marcos Application College.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_II:_Conquista_y_Virreinato2-77)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_III:_Rep%C3%BAblica3-74)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Facultad_de_Educaci%C3%B3n-80)

In 1770, the historic Real Convictorio de San Carlos was founded—merging the existing San Felipe College of Law and the San Martín College of Philosophy and Law.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_II:_Conquista_y_Virreinato2-77) On June 28, 1935, a new university statute was issued, in which it was called the Faculty of Law and Political Science.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Enciclopedia_Tem%C3%A1tica_del_Per%C3%BA._TOMO_III:_Rep%C3%BAblica3-74) It has a free legal office for its service.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Facultad_de_Derecho_y_Ciencia_Pol%C3%ADtica-81)

## Academics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Academics")]

### Admissions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Admissions")]

Admission for undergraduate studies is mainly through an [entrance examination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Educational_entrance_examination "Educational entrance examination"). Although there are ways to carry out a special exam in the case of transfers, foreigners, first places in schools, and the disabled. The most required type of exam is the one that is carried out twice a year: in March and in September.

In the case of postgraduate studies, admission is made through enrollment. As there are a limited number of vacancies, an admission exam is carried out that is prepared and graded by a special jury according to the area of study to which it is applied. In 2020, after the suspension of the first admission exam on March 12 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") and after more than six months of not applying it,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-83) the University Council decided to approve the application of the online admission exam, being the first of its kind in the history of the university, on October 2 and 3 of that same year.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-84)

### International programs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: International programs")]

The University of San Marcos is actively involved in fostering international cooperation and engagement through various academic programs, research collaborations, and global partnerships. In addition, the university has counted as a main member of the [Strategic Alliance of Peruvian Universities](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alianza%20Estrat%C3%A9gica%20(Per%C3%BA) "es:Alianza Estratégica (Perú)") with agreements to achieve exchanges of undergraduate and postgraduate students from the three main Peruvian universities—UNMSM, [UNI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_Engineering "National University of Engineering") and [UNALM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Agrarian_University "National Agrarian University")—and others Peruvian universities as associated members.

## Campuses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Campuses")]

Since its foundation, the University of San Marcos has passed through five different main locations:[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-UNMSM:_Historia2-96) From 16th to 19th centuries: the first location was located at the premises of the Convent of Nuestra Señora del Rosario of the Dominican Order; the second one was near the outskirts of San Marcelo, shortly before the Convent of the Order of San Agustín had functioned; the third—since 1575—was in the primitive Plaza del Estanque, the current location of the [Congress of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_the_Republic_of_Peru "Congress of the Republic of Peru").

In the second half of the 19th century, it was moved to the premises of the old Convictorio de San Carlos. At the end of the 19th century, the "San Fernando" Faculty of Medicine moved to its permanent location on the current Avenida Grau. Since the mid-1960s, during the government of Manuel Prado, the university began to occupy its main campus, the current Ciudad Universitaria, located between Avenida Universitaria and [Avenida Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela_Avenue "Venezuela Avenue"). The rectory, the Central Library and 17 of the 20 faculties of the university are currently located there.

### University city

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: University city")]

Since 1966, the University City of the National University of San Marcos, generally known as "University City of Lima" or simply "University City", is the main campus of the National University of San Marcos. In it are located 17 of the 20 faculties of the University of San Marcos, the Central Library, the [Stadium of the University of San Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Universidad_San_Marcos "Estadio Universidad San Marcos"), and one of the university residences. In addition, the City includes the archaeological complex of Huaca San Marcos.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Cat%C3%A1logo_Universitario_y_Prospecto_de_Admisi%C3%B3n_2011-I-97) The university has two residence halls for its two main campuses.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Cat%C3%A1logo_Universitario_y_Prospecto_de_Admisi%C3%B3n_2011-I-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Residencia_de_la_Ciudad_Universitaria-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Residencia_universitaria_Julio_C._Tello-99)

Since 2007, road works have been carried out outside the University City. The works were imposed by the former mayor, [Luis Castañeda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Casta%C3%B1eda "Luis Castañeda"), of the [Metropolitan Municipality of Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Municipality_of_Lima "Metropolitan Municipality of Lima"). In 2008, specialists from the [National University of Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_Engineering "National University of Engineering") and the CDL-College of Engineers of Peru reformulated the municipal works. The works have been stopped by a precautionary measure from the [National Institute of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_of_Culture "National Institute of Culture") (INC) after verifying that these works damaged part of the cultural heritage in the Huaca San Marcos. In January 2011, the new municipal management deemed that the operation was unnecessary.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Construcci%C3%B3n_de_anillo_vial_en_San_Marcos_fue_capricho_de_la_gesti%C3%B3n_de_Casta%C3%B1eda,_seg%C3%BAn_comuna_lime%C3%B1a2-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Ven_innecesario_anillo_vial_en_San_Marcos2-101)

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/UNMSM_P1000084.jpg/250px-UNMSM_P1000084.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UNMSM_P1000084.jpg)

Exterior view of the Central Library

The "Pedro Zulen" Central Library of the university is a 19,800 m 2 building. It has a multifunctional stage and 400 seats. The Central Library "Pedro Zulen", under the auspices of [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO"), leads the initiative to develop digitalization of publications.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Cat%C3%A1logo_Universitario_y_Prospecto_de_Admisi%C3%B3n_2011-I-97)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-San_Marcos_al_d%C3%ADa_(n%C2%B0_163):_Tesis_en_l%C3%ADnea-102) The library directs the main activity of SISBIB.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Cat%C3%A1logo_Universitario_y_Prospecto_de_Admisi%C3%B3n_2011-I-97)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Colecciones:_Bibliotecas_Especializadas-103) Each one of the faculties of the National University of San Marcos has its own library in the study areas of each faculty, these are connected to each other through the Library System (SISBIB) of the university.

#### Stadium of the University of San Marcos

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Stadium of the University of San Marcos")]

The [Stadium of the National University of San Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Universidad_San_Marcos "Estadio Universidad San Marcos"), officially known as the "Colossus of America", is located in the center of the University City. Its main accesses are through block 5 of Av. Amézaga and block 36 of Av. Venezuela. At the local level, it has been the official stadium of the university soccer team, [Club Deportivo Universidad San Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportivo_Universidad_San_Marcos "Deportivo Universidad San Marcos"), which played until 2011 in the Second Division of Peru.

It was inaugurated in 1951, commemorating the 400th anniversary of the founding of the University of San Marcos. The San Marcos stadium initially had a total capacity of 70,000 people.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Historia_del_Estadio_de_la_Universidad_Nacional_Mayor_de_San_Marcos-104) It has been conditioned to an official capacity of 32,000 people;[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-105) the remodeled venue was for the 2019 [South American U-17 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_American_U-17_Championship "South American U-17 Championship") and the [2019 Pan American Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Pan_American_Games "2019 Pan American Games").

## Culture and heritage

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Culture and heritage")]

### Cultural centers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Cultural centers")]

Currently, the National University of San Marcos has two [cultural centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_center "Cultural center") in two of its historic buildings. The [Casona de San Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casona_of_the_National_University_of_San_Marcos "Casona of the National University of San Marcos")—its main cultural center—and the Colegio Real de San Marcos.

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/CCSM-UNMSM_Casona_de_San_Marcos_y_Parque_Univesitario.jpg/250px-CCSM-UNMSM_Casona_de_San_Marcos_y_Parque_Univesitario.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CCSM-UNMSM_Casona_de_San_Marcos_y_Parque_Univesitario.jpg)

Exterior view of the Casona de San Marcos

The [Cultural Center "La Casona" of San Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casona_of_the_National_University_of_San_Marcos "Casona of the National University of San Marcos") is one of the main tourist attractions of the [Historic Center of Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historic_Centre_of_Lima "Historic Centre of Lima"). The complex is part of the area and the list of buildings in the historic center of the capital that in 1988 was declared a [World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") by [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO"). In 1989, the National University of San Marcos, the Spanish Agency for International Cooperation (AECI) and the [National Institute of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_of_Culture "National Institute of Culture") sign a Peru-Spain agreement to adapting its architectural complex for culture and artistic creation.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-El_Centro_Cultural_de_San_Marcos_y_la_antigua_Casona_del_parque_universitario_(parte_3)-117)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-El_Centro_Cultural_de_San_Marcos:_Un_horizonte_de_renovaciones-118)

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Antiguo_colegio_real_de_San_Felipe.jpg/250px-Antiguo_colegio_real_de_San_Felipe.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Antiguo_colegio_real_de_San_Felipe.jpg)

Exterior view of the Royal College

The Royal College Cultural Center of Contemporary Peruvian Cultures, established in 2006, is located in the environment of the old "Royal College" of San Marcos, next to the [Congress of the Republic of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_the_Republic_of_Peru "Congress of the Republic of Peru"). It is made up of three units of the university: the Institute of Applied Linguistics CILA, the "Domingo Angulo" Historical Archive of the University of San Marcos, and the Andean Rural History Seminar. Exhibitions and shows are regularly held.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Trabajo_Fotogr%C3%A1fico_en_Colegio_Real_de_San_Marcos-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Exposici%C3%B3n_en_Colegio_Real:_Nuestras_damas_decimon%C3%B3nicas-120)

It was founded on the initiative of [Viceroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_Peru "Viceroyalty of Peru")[Francisco Álvarez de Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_de_Toledo "Francisco de Toledo") in 1592. After the [Bourbon Reforms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourbon_Reforms "Bourbon Reforms") that led to the [expulsion of the Jesuits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suppression_of_the_Society_of_Jesus "Suppression of the Society of Jesus"), the campus was recast as the Convictorio de San Carlos. At the end of the 18th century, the War Inspector [Gabriel de Avilés y del Fierro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_de_Avil%C3%A9s,_4th_Marquis_of_Avil%C3%A9s "Gabriel de Avilés, 4th Marquis of Avilés") dedicated the premises to the headquarters of the Royal Regiment of Lima. Since the end of the 20th century, the University of San Marcos has given the Royal College the functions of a Cultural Center and Historical Archive.

### University museums

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: University museums")]

The University of San Marcos has institutions that function exclusively as museums, these are the [Museum of Natural History of Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Natural_History,_Lima "Museum of Natural History, Lima"),[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Visitas_al_Museo_de_Historia_Natural_Javier_Prado-121) the Sacaco Paleontological Museum, the Museum of Art, the Museum of Archaeology, the Historical Museum of Physical Sciences, among others.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Museo_Hist%C3%B3rico_de_Ciencias_F%C3%ADsicas-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Museo_Hist%C3%B3rico_de_Ciencias_F%C3%ADsicas_(Universidad_Nacional_Mayor_de_San_Marcos)-123) The university also has four other specialized libraries.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Bibliotecas_especializadas-124)

### Archaeological sites

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Archaeological sites")]

[![Image 34: La huaca San Marcos, anteriormente llamada Huaca Pando o Huaca Aramburú, captada por el investigador Thomas Joseph Hutchinson (1873). Forma parte del complejo Maranga. Antiguamente tenía a su frente a la huaca Concha, destruida a mediados del siglo XX.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/HuacadeSanMarcos.jpg/250px-HuacadeSanMarcos.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HuacadeSanMarcos.jpg)

The Huaca de San Marcos. It is part of the Maranga complex

The National University of San Marcos has researched various archaeological sites and historical collections, such as the Huaca de San Marcos and others of the Maranga archaeological complex. In it, various ceramics have been found, as well as spondylus and quipus. The [Ministry of Culture of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture_(Peru) "Ministry of Culture (Peru)") first declared the Huaca San Marcos and then all the minor archaeological sites on the campus, as Cultural Heritage of the Nation.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Huaca_San_Marcos-125)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Lista_completa_de_sitios_arqueol%C3%B3gicos_en_Lima-126)

In 1966, [Pablo Macera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Macera "Pablo Macera") organized a trip to the Pacopampa archaeological site in [Querocoto District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Querocoto_District "Querocoto District"); in 1970, he got Emilio Choy Ma to make a donation to San Marcos to acquire the Pacopampa Ceremonial Center.

Both formally and colloquially, the characters that have been part of the National University of San Marcos have received the title of _sanmarquinos_.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-San_Marcos_inaugura_exposici%C3%B3n_con_documentos_in%C3%A9ditos_de_personajes_ilustres-127)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-San_Marcos_inaugura_exposici%C3%B3n_sobre_egresados_ilustres_por_su_468_aniversario-128) The word has been in common use by the Peruvian population to refer to the close and prominent figures of this house of studies, and even to the pets and animals adopted by the university community.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Mario_Vargas_Llosa_lleg%C3%B3_a_Lima_para_sumarse_a_la_FIL_Lima_2019-129)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Mario_Vargas_Llosa_ya_se_encuentra_en_Lima_para_la_FIL_2019-130)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Muri%C3%B3_Perrovaca,_la_popular_mascota_de_San_Marcos-131)

## Athletics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_University_of_San_Marcos&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Athletics")]

On August 7, 1924, San Marcos students founded the University Sports Federation of Peru. Since 1936, this federation has organized the National University Sports Games, the Regional University Sports Games and the National University Championships. Since 1963, it has participated in the [Universiade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universiade "Universiade").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Federaci%C3%B3n_deportiva_universitaria_del_Per%C3%BA:_Historia-132) The basketball team had participated in the [Lima Basketball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_de_Basket_de_Lima "Liga de Basket de Lima").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-San_Marcos_Basket-133)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Divisi%C3%B3n_Superior_Varones-134)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Divisi%C3%B3n_Superior_Damas-135)

The University of San Marcos has had various professional football teams, including the University Football Federation ([Club Universitario de Deportes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Universitario_de_Deportes "Club Universitario de Deportes")) that was founded in 1924 by students until it was separated from the university and became private due to problems with the authorities in 1932; and the [Deportivo Universidad San Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportivo_Universidad_San_Marcos "Deportivo Universidad San Marcos") that came to dispute the second division until 2012.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Club_UNMSM-136)

The first university Games were held in 1936 in the city of Lima. Since then, four years between each Games was marked, though, recently, they have been taking place every 2 years. In 1951, the [Stadium of the University of San Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Universidad_San_Marcos "Estadio Universidad San Marcos") was inaugurated in the center of the main campus.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos#cite_note-Federaci%C3%B3n_deportiva_universitaria_del_Per%C3%BA:_Cronolog%C3%ADa-137) For the celebration of the [2019 Pan American Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Pan_American_Games "2019 Pan American Games"), the Organizing Committee of [Lima 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Pan_American_Games "2019 Pan American Games") chose various sports facilities located between the city of Lima, as well as in Callao, as Pan American venues.
