**George Walker Bush**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-1) (born July 6, 1946) is an American politician, businessman, and retired [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") officer who served as the 43rd [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") from 2001 to 2009. A member of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), he served as the 46th [governor of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Texas "Governor of Texas") from 1995 to 2000. He is the eldest son of [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush"), the 41st president of the United States.

Born into the prominent [Bush family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_family "Bush family") in [New Haven, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Haven,_Connecticut "New Haven, Connecticut"), Bush flew warplanes in the [Texas Air National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Air_National_Guard "Texas Air National Guard") in his twenties. After graduating from [Harvard Business School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Business_School "Harvard Business School") in 1975, he worked in the oil industry. He later co-owned the [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball") team [Texas Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Rangers_(baseball) "Texas Rangers (baseball)") before being elected governor of Texas [in 1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Texas_gubernatorial_election "1994 Texas gubernatorial election"). [As governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governorship_of_George_W._Bush "Governorship of George W. Bush"), Bush successfully sponsored legislation for [tort reform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tort_reform "Tort reform"), increased education funding, set higher standards for schools, and reformed the criminal justice system. He also helped make Texas the [leading producer of wind-generated electricity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_power_in_Texas "Wind power in Texas") in the United States. In the [2000 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election "2000 United States presidential election"), he defeated Democratic incumbent vice president [Al Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore "Al Gore") while [losing the popular vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_presidential_elections_in_which_the_winner_lost_the_popular_vote "List of United States presidential elections in which the winner lost the popular vote") after a narrow and contested [United States Electoral College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Electoral_College "United States Electoral College") win, which involved the Supreme Court decision _[Bush v. Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush\_v.\_Gore "Bush v. Gore")_ to stop [a recount in Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election_recount_in_Florida "2000 United States presidential election recount in Florida").

In his first term, Bush signed [a major tax-cut program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_tax_cuts "Bush tax cuts") and an education-reform bill, the [No Child Left Behind Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Child_Left_Behind_Act "No Child Left Behind Act"). He pushed for socially conservative efforts such as the [Partial-Birth Abortion Ban Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial-Birth_Abortion_Ban_Act "Partial-Birth Abortion Ban Act"), restrictions on same-sex marriage, and [faith-based initiatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith-based_initiatives "Faith-based initiatives"). He also initiated the [President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President's_Emergency_Plan_for_AIDS_Relief "President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief"), in 2003, to address the global [AIDS epidemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AIDS_epidemic "AIDS epidemic"). The [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks") during 2001 decisively reshaped his administration, resulting in the start of the [war on terror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_terror "War on terror") and the creation of the [Department of Homeland Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Homeland_Security "Department of Homeland Security"). Bush ordered the [invasion of Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_invasion_of_Afghanistan "United States invasion of Afghanistan") in an effort to overthrow the [Taliban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban "Taliban"), destroy [al-Qaeda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda "Al-Qaeda"), and capture [Osama bin Laden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osama_bin_Laden "Osama bin Laden"). He signed the [Patriot Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot_Act "Patriot Act"), expanding surveillance powers for suspected terrorists. He also ordered the [2003 invasion of Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq "2003 invasion of Iraq") to overthrow [Saddam Hussein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein "Saddam Hussein")'s regime, citing claims that it [possessed weapons of mass destruction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction "Iraq and weapons of mass destruction") and had [ties with al-Qaeda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein_and_al-Qaeda_link_allegations "Saddam Hussein and al-Qaeda link allegations"). Bush later signed the [Medicare Modernization Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicare_Prescription_Drug,_Improvement,_and_Modernization_Act "Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act"), which created [Medicare Part D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicare_Part_D "Medicare Part D"). In 2004, Bush [was re-elected president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election "2004 United States presidential election") in a close race, beating Democratic opponent [John Kerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry") and winning the popular vote.

During his second term, Bush negotiated various [free trade agreements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_trade_agreement "Free trade agreement"), appointed [John Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Roberts "John Roberts") and [Samuel Alito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Alito "Samuel Alito") to the Supreme Court, and sought major changes to [Social Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Security_(United_States) "Social Security (United States)") and immigration laws, both of which ultimately failed in Congress. He was widely criticized for [his administration's handling of Hurricane Katrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criticism_of_the_government_response_to_Hurricane_Katrina "Criticism of the government response to Hurricane Katrina") and revelations of [torture against detainees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Ghraib_torture_and_prisoner_abuse "Abu Ghraib torture and prisoner abuse") at [Abu Ghraib prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Ghraib_prison "Abu Ghraib prison") in Iraq. Amid his unpopularity, the Democrats regained control of Congress in the [2006 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_United_States_elections "2006 United States elections"). In January 2007, Bush launched [a surge of troops in Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War_troop_surge_of_2007 "Iraq War troop surge of 2007"). As his presidency came to a close, the country experienced [a financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis "2008 financial crisis"), resulting in the [Great Recession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Recession "Great Recession"), prompting his administration and Congress to push through emergency economic measures aimed at stabilizing the financial system, including the [Troubled Asset Relief Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubled_Asset_Relief_Program "Troubled Asset Relief Program").

After his second term, Bush returned to Texas, where he has maintained a low public profile. At various points in his presidency, he was both among the most popular and among the least popular presidents in U.S. history. He received the highest recorded approval ratings in the wake of the September 11 attacks, and one of the lowest ratings during the 2008 financial crisis. Bush left office as one of the most unpopular U.S. presidents; however, [public opinion of him](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_image_of_George_W._Bush "Public image of George W. Bush") has improved in [his post-presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-presidency_of_George_W._Bush "Post-presidency of George W. Bush"). [Scholars and historians generally rank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_presidents_of_the_United_States "Historical rankings of presidents of the United States") Bush as a below-average president.

## Early life and education

Main article: [Early life of George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_of_George_W._Bush "Early life of George W. Bush")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/George_and_Barbara_Bush_with_their_first_born_child_George_W._Bush%2C_while_Bush_was_a_student_at_Yale.jpg/250px-George_and_Barbara_Bush_with_their_first_born_child_George_W._Bush%2C_while_Bush_was_a_student_at_Yale.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:George_and_Barbara_Bush_with_their_first_born_child_George_W._Bush,_while_Bush_was_a_student_at_Yale.jpg)

George W. Bush with his parents, [Barbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Bush "Barbara Bush") and [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") in 1947

George Walker Bush was born on July 6, 1946, at [Grace-New Haven Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace-New_Haven_Hospital "Grace-New Haven Hospital") in [New Haven, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Haven,_Connecticut "New Haven, Connecticut").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-2) He is the first child of [George Herbert Walker Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Herbert_Walker_Bush "George Herbert Walker Bush") and [Barbara Pierce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Pierce "Barbara Pierce"), and was raised in [Midland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midland,_Texas "Midland, Texas") and [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"), Texas. His five siblings are [Robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Robinson_Bush "Pauline Robinson Bush"), [Jeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Bush "Jeb Bush"), [Neil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Bush "Neil Bush"), [Marvin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Bush "Marvin Bush") and [Dorothy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Bush_Koch "Dorothy Bush Koch"). Robin died from [leukemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leukemia "Leukemia") at the age of three in 1953.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-3) His paternal grandfather, [Prescott Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prescott_Bush "Prescott Bush"), was a U.S. senator from [Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut "Connecticut").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-4) His father was [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan")'s vice president from 1981 to 1989 and the 41st president of the United States from 1989 to 1993. Bush has distant [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Americans "English Americans") and [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Americans "German Americans") ancestry, along with more distant (over 7-generations removed) [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Americans "Dutch Americans"), [Welsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_Americans "Welsh Americans"), [Irish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Americans "Irish Americans"), [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Americans "French Americans"), and [Scottish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Americans "Scottish Americans") roots.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-5)

Bush attended public schools in Midland, Texas, until the family moved to Houston after he had completed seventh grade. He then spent two years at [The Kinkaid School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kinkaid_School "The Kinkaid School"), a [college-preparatory school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College-preparatory_school "College-preparatory school") in [Piney Point Village, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piney_Point_Village,_Texas "Piney Point Village, Texas").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-6)

Bush later attended [Phillips Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phillips_Academy "Phillips Academy"), a boarding school in [Andover, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andover,_Massachusetts "Andover, Massachusetts"), where he played baseball and was the head cheerleader during his senior year.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-8) He attended [Yale University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University "Yale University") from 1964 to 1968, graduating with a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") degree in history.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-whitehousebio-9) During this time, he was a cheerleader and a member of the [Delta Kappa Epsilon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Kappa_Epsilon "Delta Kappa Epsilon"), serving as the president of the fraternity during his senior year.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-12) Bush became [a member](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Skull_and_Bones_members "List of Skull and Bones members") of the [Skull and Bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull_and_Bones "Skull and Bones") society as a senior.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-13) Bush was a [rugby union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_union "Rugby union") player and was on Yale's 1st XV.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-14) He characterized himself as an average student.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-15) His [grade point average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_point_average "Grade point average") during his first three years at Yale was 77, and he had a similar average under a nonnumerical rating system in his final year.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-16)

In the fall of 1973, Bush entered [Harvard Business School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Business_School "Harvard Business School"). He graduated in 1975 with a [Master of Business Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration "Master of Business Administration"). He is the only U.S. president to have earned that degree.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-17)

## Career

### Military career

Main article: [George W. Bush military service controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush_military_service_controversy "George W. Bush military service controversy")

See also: [Killian documents controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killian_documents_controversy "Killian documents controversy") and [Killian documents authenticity issues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killian_documents_authenticity_issues "Killian documents authenticity issues")

In May 1968, Bush joined the [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") and was commissioned into the [Texas Air National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Air_National_Guard "Texas Air National Guard").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-wpbushguardquestion-18) After two years of training in active-duty service,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-lardner19990728-19) he was assigned to [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"), flying [Convair F-102s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convair_F-102 "Convair F-102") with the [147th Reconnaissance Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/147th_Reconnaissance_Wing "147th Reconnaissance Wing") out of [Ellington Field Joint Reserve Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellington_Field_Joint_Reserve_Base "Ellington Field Joint Reserve Base").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-wpbushguardquestion-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-20) Critics, including former [Democratic National Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Committee "Democratic National Committee") Chairman [Terry McAuliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_McAuliffe "Terry McAuliffe"), have alleged that Bush was favorably treated due to his father's political standing as a member of [the House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives"), citing his selection as a pilot despite his low pilot aptitude test scores and his irregular attendance.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-wpbushguardquestion-18) In June 2005, [the Department of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense "United States Department of Defense") released all the records of Bush's Texas Air National Guard service, which remain in its official archives.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-USDoDbushrecords-21)

In late 1972 and early 1973, he drilled with the [187th Fighter Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/187th_Fighter_Wing "187th Fighter Wing") of the [Alabama Air National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_Air_National_Guard "Alabama Air National Guard"). He had moved to [Montgomery, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montgomery,_Alabama "Montgomery, Alabama"), to work on the unsuccessful U.S. Senate campaign of Republican [Winton M. Blount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winton_M._Blount "Winton M. Blount").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-22)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-23) In 1972, Bush was suspended from flying for failure to take a scheduled physical exam.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-24) He was honorably discharged from the [Air Force Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_Reserve "Air Force Reserve") on November 21, 1974.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-25)

Bush remains the most recent president to have served in the military.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-26)

### Business career

Main article: [Professional life of George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_life_of_George_W._Bush "Professional life of George W. Bush")

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Gerald_Ford_greets_George_W._Bush.jpg/250px-Gerald_Ford_greets_George_W._Bush.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gerald_Ford_greets_George_W._Bush.jpg)

Bush with former president [Gerald Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford "Gerald Ford") in August 1984

In 1977, Bush established [Arbusto Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arbusto_Energy "Arbusto Energy"), a small [oil exploration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_exploration "Oil exploration") company, which began operations in 1978.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-Lardner-27)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-28) He later changed the name to Bush Exploration. In 1984, his company merged with the larger [Spectrum 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectrum_7 "Spectrum 7"), and Bush became chairman. The company was hurt by decreased oil prices, and it folded into [Harken Energy Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harken_Energy_Corporation "Harken Energy Corporation"),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-29) with Bush becoming a member of Harken's board of directors. Questions of [possible insider trading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush_insider_trading_allegations "George W. Bush insider trading allegations") involving Harken arose, but a [Securities and Exchange Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Securities_and_Exchange_Commission "Securities and Exchange Commission") investigation concluded that the information Bush had at the time of his stock sale was not sufficient to constitute insider trading.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-30)

In April 1989, Bush arranged for a group of investors to purchase a controlling interest of Major League Baseball's [Texas Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Rangers_(baseball) "Texas Rangers (baseball)") for $89 million and invested $500,000 himself to start. He then was managing general partner for five years.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-TexRngrs-31) He actively led the team's projects and regularly attended its games, often choosing to sit in the open stands with fans.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-32) Bush's sale of his shares in the Rangers in 1998 brought him over $15 million from his initial $800,000 investment.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-33)

In the early or mid 1990s, before his gubernatorial campaign, Bush briefly considered a candidacy to become the [Commissioner of Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commissioner_of_Baseball "Commissioner of Baseball").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-35)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-36)

### Early political involvement

[In 1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "1978 United States House of Representatives elections"), Bush ran for the [U.S. House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_of_Representatives "U.S. House of Representatives") from [Texas's 19th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_19th_congressional_district "Texas's 19th congressional district"). The retiring member, [George H. Mahon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._Mahon "George H. Mahon"), had held the district for the Democratic Party since 1935. Bush's opponent, [Kent Hance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent_Hance "Kent Hance"), portrayed him as out of touch with rural Texans, and Bush lost the election, receiving 46.8 percent of the vote to Hance's 53.2 percent.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-NewsMine-37)

Bush and his family moved to Washington, D.C., in 1988 to work on [his father's campaign for the U.S. presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush_1988_presidential_campaign "George H. W. Bush 1988 presidential campaign").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-38)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-39) He was a campaign advisor and liaison to the media, and assisted his father by campaigning across the country.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40) In December 1991, Bush was one of seven people named by his father to run his father's 1992 presidential [re-election campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush_1992_presidential_campaign "George H. W. Bush 1992 presidential campaign") as a campaign advisor.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-41) The previous month, his father had asked him to tell White House chief of staff [John H. Sununu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_H._Sununu "John H. Sununu") to resign.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-42)

## Governor of Texas (1995–2000)

Main article: [Governorship of George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governorship_of_George_W._Bush "Governorship of George W. Bush")

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/George_Bush_45_%2849492156502%29.jpg/250px-George_Bush_45_%2849492156502%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:George_Bush_45_(49492156502).jpg)

Bush during his governorship, 1999

Bush declared his candidacy for the [1994 Texas gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Texas_gubernatorial_election "1994 Texas gubernatorial election") at the same time his brother Jeb [sought the governorship in Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Florida_gubernatorial_election "1994 Florida gubernatorial election"). His campaign focused on four themes: welfare reform, [tort reform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tort_reform "Tort reform"), crime reduction, and education improvement.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40) Bush's campaign advisers were [Karen Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_Hughes "Karen Hughes"), [Joe Allbaugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Allbaugh "Joe Allbaugh"), and [Karl Rove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Rove "Karl Rove").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-SlaterBrain-43)

After easily winning the Republican primary, Bush faced popular Democratic incumbent governor [Ann Richards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Richards "Ann Richards").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-telegraph-44) In the course of the campaign, Bush pledged to sign a bill allowing Texans to obtain [permits to carry concealed weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concealed_carry_permit "Concealed carry permit"). Richards had vetoed the bill, but Bush signed it into law after he became governor.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-concealed_carry-45) According to _[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Atlantic "The Atlantic")_, the race "featured a rumor that she was a lesbian, along with a rare instance of such a tactic's making it into the public record – when a regional chairman of the Bush campaign allowed himself, perhaps inadvertently, to be quoted criticizing Richards for 'appointing avowed [homosexual activists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_social_movements "LGBT social movements")' to state jobs".[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-46)_The Atlantic_, and others, connected the lesbian rumor to Karl Rove,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-47) but Rove denied being involved.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-48) Bush won the general election with 53.5 percent of the vote against Richards' 45.9 percent.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-49)

Bush used a budget surplus to push through Texas's largest [tax cut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_cut "Tax cut"), $2 billion.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-SlaterBrain-43) He extended government funding for organizations providing education on the dangers of alcohol and [drug use and abuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substance_abuse "Substance abuse"), and helping to reduce [domestic violence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_violence "Domestic violence").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-50) His administration lowered the age at which juveniles can be sent to adult court for serious crimes to 14.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-51) Bush presided over 152 executions,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-52) more than any previous governor in modern American history; critics such as [Helen Prejean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Prejean "Helen Prejean") argue that he failed to give serious consideration to [clemency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clemency "Clemency") requests.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-executions-53)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-54) Critics also contended that during his tenure, Texas ranked near the bottom in environmental evaluations. Supporters pointed to his efforts to raise the salaries of teachers and improve educational test scores.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40)

In 1999, Bush signed [a law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renewable_portfolio_standard "Renewable portfolio standard") that required electric retailers to buy a certain amount of energy from renewable sources (RPS),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-txlaw-55)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-56)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-57) which helped [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_power_in_Texas "Wind power in Texas") eventually become the leading producer of [wind-powered electricity in the U.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_power_in_the_United_States "Wind power in the United States")[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-58)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-mighty_wind-59)

[In 1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_Texas_gubernatorial_election "1998 Texas gubernatorial election"), Bush won re-election with a record[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40) 68 percent of the vote.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-60) He became the first governor in Texas history to be elected to two consecutive four-year terms.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40) During his second term, Bush promoted faith-based organizations and enjoyed high [approval ratings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Approval_rating "Approval rating"), which ranged between 62 and 81 percent.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-61) He proclaimed June 10, 2000, to be [Jesus Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Day "Jesus Day") in Texas, a day on which he urged all Texans to "answer the call to serve those in need".[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-62)

Throughout Bush's first term, he was the focus of national attention as a potential future presidential candidate. Following his re-election, speculation soared, and within a year he decided to seek the 2000 Republican presidential nomination.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40)

## Presidential campaigns

### 2000 presidential campaign

Main articles: [George W. Bush 2000 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush_2000_presidential_campaign "George W. Bush 2000 presidential campaign"), [2000 Republican Party presidential primaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries "2000 Republican Party presidential primaries"), and [2000 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election "2000 United States presidential election")

#### Primary

Bush portrayed himself as a [compassionate conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compassionate_conservative "Compassionate conservative"), implying he was more centrist than other Republicans. He campaigned on a platform which included bringing integrity and honor back to the White House, increasing the size of the military, cutting taxes, improving education, and aiding minorities.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40) By early 2000, the race had centered on Bush and Arizona senator [John McCain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain "John McCain").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40)

Bush won the [Iowa caucuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa_caucuses "Iowa caucuses") and, although heavily favored to win the [New Hampshire primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire_primary "New Hampshire primary"), trailed McCain by 19% and lost. Despite this, he regained momentum and effectively became the front runner after the [South Carolina primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_presidential_primaries,_2000 "Republican Party presidential primaries, 2000"), which according to _[The Boston Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boston\_Globe "The Boston Globe")_ made history for his campaign's negativity. _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ described it as a [smear campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smear_campaign "Smear campaign").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-anatomy-63)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-64)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-65)

#### General election

On July 25, 2000, Bush surprised some observers when he selected [Dick Cheney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Cheney "Dick Cheney")–a former [White House chief of staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_chief_of_staff "White House chief of staff"), U.S. representative, and secretary of defense–to be his running mate. At the time, Cheney was serving as head of Bush's vice presidential search committee. Soon after at the [2000 Republican National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Republican_National_Convention "2000 Republican National Convention"), Bush and Cheney were officially nominated by the Republican Party.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-66)

Bush continued to campaign across the country and touted his record as Governor of Texas.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40) During his campaign, Bush criticized his Democratic opponent, incumbent vice president [Al Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore "Al Gore"), over [gun control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_law_in_the_United_States "Gun law in the United States") and taxation.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-67)

When the election returns were tallied on November 7, Bush had won 29 states, including Florida. The closeness of the Florida outcome led to [a recount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election_in_Florida,_2000 "United States presidential election in Florida, 2000").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40) The initial recount also went to Bush, but the outcome was tied up in lower courts for a month until eventually reaching the [U.S. Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Supreme_Court "U.S. Supreme Court").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-68) On December 9, in the controversial _[Bush v. Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush\_v.\_Gore "Bush v. Gore")_ ruling,[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-69) the Court reversed a [Florida Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Supreme_Court "Florida Supreme Court") decision that had ordered a third count, and stopped an ordered statewide hand recount based on the argument that the use of different standards among Florida's counties violated the [Equal Protection Clause](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equal_Protection_Clause "Equal Protection Clause") of the [Fourteenth Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40) The machine recount showed that Bush had won the Florida vote by a margin of 537 votes out of six million casts.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-2000results-70) Although he had received 543,895 fewer individual nationwide votes than Gore, Bush won the election, receiving 271 [electoral votes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electoral_College_(United_States) "Electoral College (United States)") to Gore's 266 (Gore had actually been awarded 267 votes by the states pledged to him plus the District of Columbia, but one D.C. elector abstained). Bush was the first person to [win a U.S. presidential election with fewer popular votes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_presidential_elections_in_which_the_winner_lost_the_popular_vote "List of United States presidential elections in which the winner lost the popular vote") than another candidate since [Benjamin Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Harrison "Benjamin Harrison") in 1888.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-2000results-70)

### 2004 presidential campaign

Main articles: [George W. Bush 2004 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush_2004_presidential_campaign "George W. Bush 2004 presidential campaign"), [2004 Republican Party presidential primaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries "2004 Republican Party presidential primaries"), and [2004 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election "2004 United States presidential election")

In his 2004 bid for re-election, Bush commanded broad support in the Republican Party and did not encounter a primary challenge. He appointed [Ken Mehlman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Mehlman "Ken Mehlman") as campaign manager, and [Karl Rove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Rove "Karl Rove") devised a political strategy.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-71) Bush and the Republican platform emphasized a strong commitment to the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-platform04-72) support for the [USA PATRIOT Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_PATRIOT_Act "USA PATRIOT Act"),[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-73) a renewed shift in policy for constitutional amendments banning abortion and [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage"),[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-platform04-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-74) reforming [Social Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Security_(United_States) "Social Security (United States)") to create private investment accounts,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-platform04-72) creation of an [ownership society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ownership_society "Ownership society"),[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-platform04-72) and opposing mandatory carbon emissions controls.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-75) Bush also called for the implementation of a [guest worker program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guest_worker_program "Guest worker program") for immigrants,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-platform04-72) which was criticized by conservatives.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-76)

The Bush campaign advertised across the U.S. against Democratic candidates, including Bush's emerging opponent, Massachusetts senator [John Kerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry"). Kerry and other Democrats attacked Bush on the [Iraq War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War "Iraq War"), and accused him of failing to stimulate the economy and job growth. The Bush campaign portrayed Kerry as a staunch [liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberalism_in_the_United_States "Liberalism in the United States") who would raise taxes and increase the size of government. The Bush campaign continuously criticized Kerry's seemingly contradictory statements on the war in Iraq,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40) and argued that Kerry lacked the decisiveness and vision necessary for success in the war on terror.

Following the resignation of CIA director [George Tenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tenet "George Tenet") in 2004, Bush nominated [Porter Goss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porter_Goss "Porter Goss") to head the agency. The White House ordered Goss to purge agency officers who were disloyal to the administration.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-salon-77) After Goss' appointment, many of the CIA's senior agents were fired or quit. The CIA has been accused of deliberately leaking classified information to undermine the 2004 election.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-wapo-78)

In the election, Bush carried 31 of 50 states, receiving 286 electoral votes. He won an absolute majority of the popular vote (50.7% to Kerry's 48.3%).[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-16_years-79)

Bush takes [the oath of office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oath_of_office_of_the_President_of_the_United_States "Oath of office of the President of the United States") administered by [Chief Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Justice_of_the_United_States "Chief Justice of the United States")[William Rehnquist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Rehnquist "William Rehnquist") at [the Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Capitol "United States Capitol") on January 20, 2001.

Bush takes the oath of office to a second term.

Bush had originally outlined an ambitious domestic agenda, but his priorities were significantly altered following the [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-80) Wars were begun in Afghanistan and Iraq, and there were significant domestic debates regarding immigration, healthcare, Social Security, economic policy, and treatment of terrorist detainees. Over an eight-year period, Bush's once-high approval ratings[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-gallup_high-81) steadily declined, while his disapproval numbers increased significantly.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-wapo_ratings-82) In 2007, the United States entered the longest post-[World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") recession.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-longest1-83)

### Domestic policy

Main article: [Domestic policy of the George W. Bush administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_policy_of_the_George_W._Bush_administration "Domestic policy of the George W. Bush administration")

#### Economic policy

Main article: [Economic policy of the George W. Bush administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_policy_of_the_George_W._Bush_administration "Economic policy of the George W. Bush administration")

Bush took office during an economic recession in the wake of the bursting of the [dot-com bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot-com_bubble "Dot-com bubble").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-84) The September 11 terrorist attacks also [impacted the economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_effects_of_the_September_11_attacks "Economic effects of the September 11 attacks").

His administration increased federal [government spending](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_spending "Government spending") from $1.8 trillion to $3 trillion (66%), while revenues increased from $2 trillion to $2.5 trillion (from 2000 to 2008). Individual income tax revenues increased by 14%, corporate tax revenues by 50%, and customs and duties by 40%. Discretionary defense spending was increased by 107%, discretionary domestic spending by 62%, Medicare spending by 131%, social security by 51%, and income security spending by 130%. Cyclically adjusted, revenues rose by 35% and spending by 65%.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-85) The increase in spending was more than under any predecessor since [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-86) The number of [economic regulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_regulation "Economic regulation") governmental workers increased by 91,196.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-bushregulation-87)

The surplus in 2000 was $237 billion–the third consecutive surplus and the largest surplus ever.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-omb-88) In 2001, Bush's budget estimated that there would be a $5.6 trillion surplus over the next ten years.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-89) Facing congressional opposition, Bush held town hall-style meetings across the U.S. to increase public support for his plan for [a $1.35 trillion tax cut program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_Growth_and_Tax_Relief_Reconciliation_Act_of_2001 "Economic Growth and Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2001"), one of the largest tax cuts in history.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40) Bush argued that unspent government funds should be returned to taxpayers, saying "the surplus is not the government's money. The surplus is the people's money."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40) Federal Reserve chairman [Alan Greenspan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Greenspan "Alan Greenspan") warned of a recession and Bush stated that a tax cut would stimulate the economy and create jobs.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-90) Treasury Secretary [Paul H. O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_H._O'Neill "Paul H. O'Neill") opposed some of the tax cuts on the basis they would contribute to budget deficits and undermine [Social Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Security_(United_States) "Social Security (United States)").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-91) O'Neill disputes the claim, made in Bush's book _Decision Points_, that he never openly disagreed with him on planned tax cuts.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-92) By 2003, the economy showed signs of improvement, though job growth remained stagnant.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-msn-40)[Another tax cut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jobs_and_Growth_Tax_Relief_Reconciliation_Act_of_2003 "Jobs and Growth Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2003") was passed that year.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-93)

Between 2001 and 2008, GDP grew at an average annual rate of 2.125%,[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-94) less than for past business cycles.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-Price_&_Ratner-95) Bush entered office with the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dow_Jones_Industrial_Average "Dow Jones Industrial Average") at 10,587, and the average peaked in October 2007 at over 14,000. When Bush left office, the average was at 7,949, one of the lowest levels of his presidency.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-96) Only four other U.S. presidents have left office with the stock market lower than when they began.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-97)

Unemployment originally rose from 4.2% in January 2001 to 6.3% in June 2003, but subsequently dropped to 4.5% in July 2007.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-98) Adjusted for inflation, [median household income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Median_household_income "Median household income") dropped by $1,175 between 2000 and 2007,[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-99) while Professor Ken Homa of [Georgetown University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_University "Georgetown University") noted that "Median real after-tax household income went up two percent".[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-100) The poverty rate increased from 11.3% in 2000 to 12.3% in 2006 after peaking at 12.7% in 2004.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-101) By October 2008, due to increases in spending,[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-greenburg-102):273 the [U.S. national debt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_debt_of_the_United_States "National debt of the United States") had risen to $11.3 trillion,[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-103) more than doubling it since 2000.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-104)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-105)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable\_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_] Most debt was accumulated as a result of what became known as the "[Bush tax cuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_tax_cuts "Bush tax cuts")" and increased national security spending.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-106) In March 2006, then-senator [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") said when he voted against raising the [debt ceiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_debt_ceiling "United States debt ceiling"): "The fact that we are here today to debate raising America's debt limit is a sign of leadership failure."[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-107) By the end of Bush's presidency, unemployment climbed to 7.2%.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-108)

#### 2008 financial crisis

In December 2007, the United States entered the longest post–[World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") recession,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-longest1-83)[caused](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Causes_of_the_Great_Recession "Causes of the Great Recession") by a [housing market correction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_housing_market_correction "United States housing market correction"), a [subprime mortgage crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subprime_mortgage_crisis "Subprime mortgage crisis"), [soaring oil prices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000s_energy_crisis "2000s energy crisis"), and other factors. In February 2008, 63,000 jobs were lost, a five-year record,[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-109) and in November, over 500,000 jobs were lost, which marked the largest loss of jobs in the United States in 34 years.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-110) The [Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Labor_Statistics "Bureau of Labor Statistics") reported that in the last four months of 2008, 1.9 million jobs were lost.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-111) By the end of 2008, the U.S. had lost 2.6 million jobs.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-112)

To aid with the situation, Bush signed a $170 billion economic stimulus package which was intended to improve the economic situation by sending tax rebate checks to many Americans and providing tax breaks for struggling businesses.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-113) The Bush administration pushed for significantly increased regulation of [Fannie Mae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fannie_Mae "Fannie Mae") and [Freddie Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mac "Freddie Mac") in 2003,[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-114) and after two years, the regulations passed the House but died in the Senate. Many Republican senators, as well as influential members of the Bush Administration, feared that the agency created by these regulations would merely be mimicking the private sector's risky practices.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-115)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-admin_crisis-116)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-117) In September 2008, the [2008 financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis "2008 financial crisis") intensified, beginning with the [Federal takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_takeover_of_Fannie_Mae_and_Freddie_Mac "Federal takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac") followed by the [bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bankruptcy_of_Lehman_Brothers "Bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers") and a federal bailout of [American International Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_International_Group "American International Group") for $85 billion.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-118)

#### Education and public health

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/No_Child_Left_Behind_Act.jpg/250px-No_Child_Left_Behind_Act.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:No_Child_Left_Behind_Act.jpg)

Funding for the NIH was cut in 2006, the first such cut in 36 years, due to rising inflation.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-123)

On November 1, 2005, Bush launched a _National Strategy for [Pandemic Influenza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flu\_pandemic "Flu pandemic")_, which culminated in an implementation plan published by the Homeland Security Council in May 2006.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-129)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-130)

After being re-elected, Bush signed into law a [Medicare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicare_(United_States) "Medicare (United States)") drug benefit program which, according to [Jan Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Crawford "Jan Crawford"), resulted in "the greatest expansion in America's [welfare state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_state "Welfare state") in forty years" – the bill's costs approached $7 trillion.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-greenburg-102):274 In 2007, Bush opposed and vetoed [State Children's Health Insurance Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Children's_Health_Insurance_Program "State Children's Health Insurance Program") (SCHIP) legislation, which was added by the Democrats onto a war funding bill and passed by Congress. It was to be funded by an increase in the cigarette tax.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-131) Bush viewed the legislation as a move toward [socialized health care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialized_health_care "Socialized health care"), and asserted that the program could benefit families making as much as $83,000 per year who did not need the help.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush#cite_note-132)

**Paniqui** ([[pɐnɪˈki]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Tagalog "Help:IPA/Tagalog")), officially the **Municipality of Paniqui** ([Ilocano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilocano_language "Ilocano language"): _Ili ti Paniqui_; [Kapampangan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapampangan_language "Kapampangan language"): _Balen ning Paniqui_; [Pangasinan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pangasinan_language "Pangasinan language"): _Baley na Paniqui_; [Tagalog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagalog_language "Tagalog language"): _Bayan ng Paniqui_), is a [municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipality_of_the_Philippines "Municipality of the Philippines") in the [province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Province "Philippine Province") of [Tarlac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarlac "Tarlac"), [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"). According to the 2024 census, it has a population of 106,190 people.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&oldid=1371559644#cite_note-5)

The town is known as the birthplace of Corazon Aquino, the [11th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_Philippines "List of presidents of the Philippines")[President of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Philippines "President of the Philippines").

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

Paniqui is an [Ilocanized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanicization "Hispanicization") term derived from the Ilocano word "_Panpaniki_" which means "[bat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bat "Bat")",[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&oldid=1371559644#cite_note-6) since the town has caves that house bats.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 13: icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/60px-Question_book-new.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Question_book-new.svg)This section **relies on a [single source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_with_a_single_source "Wikipedia:Articles with a single source")**. Unsourced material may be challenged and [removed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Burden_of_evidence "Wikipedia:Verifiability").  
_Find sources:_["Paniqui"](https://www.google.com/search?as_eq=wikipedia&q=%22Paniqui%22)–[news](https://www.google.com/search?tbm=nws&q=%22Paniqui%22+-wikipedia&tbs=ar:1)**·**[newspapers](https://www.google.com/search?&q=%22Paniqui%22&tbs=bkt:s&tbm=bks)**·**[books](https://www.google.com/search?tbs=bks:1&q=%22Paniqui%22+-wikipedia)**·**[scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Paniqui%22)**·**[JSTOR](https://www.jstor.org/action/doBasicSearch?Query=%22Paniqui%22&acc=on&wc=on)_(November 2022)_ _([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance\_template\_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_

The birth of Paniqui could be traced way back in 1712 when the provincial government of [Pangasinan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pangasinan "Pangasinan") sent a group of men south of [Bayambang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayambang "Bayambang"), [Pangasinan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pangasinan "Pangasinan") for the expansion of the Christian faith. The pioneering group was led by two brothers, Raymundo and Manuel Paragas of [Dagupan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dagupan "Dagupan") and established the Local Government in a Sitio called "manggang marikit" (mango of an unmarried woman). Surprisingly, in this sitio, there is a great number of mammals called by Ilocanos "pampaniki" and it was from this term that the name Paniqui was derived.

An uprising led by Caragay during the early part of 1720 forced the Local Government in "manggang marikit" to abandon the place and to evacuate for lowland called "Acocolao", a place 2 kilometers (1.2 mi) west of the present Poblacion. It was a historical sitio where the first Filipino Moro, Sultan Ali Mudin, was [baptized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptism "Baptism") in 1750.

Paniqui was a sprawling town that covered a wide area that time. Some of the barrios that formerly comprised Paniqui were "San Roque", now [Cuyapo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuyapo "Cuyapo"); "Barong", now [Gerona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerona,_Tarlac "Gerona, Tarlac"); "San Jose De Camiling", now [Camiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camiling "Camiling"); "Bani", now [Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramos,_Tarlac "Ramos, Tarlac"); "San Ramon", now [Moncada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moncada,_Tarlac "Moncada, Tarlac"); and [Anao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anao,_Tarlac "Anao, Tarlac").

The period between 1750 and 1896 were painful years of Spanish tyranny and oppression because the insurrectos and sometimes bandits, who are conveniently sprouted among the people, made sporadic attacks upon the [conquistadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistadores "Conquistadores"). These attacks on the Spaniards, who came on the islands bringing the sword and the cross, were marred by cholera and smallpox epidemics punctuated by floods and typhoons.

However, a group of Paniqui [patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriotism "Patriotism"), welded together by a common belief of oneness, unselfish devotion for freedom and who were spurred by ruthless Spanish tyranny, organized a legitimate segment of the [Katipunan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katipunan "Katipunan") on January 12, 1896, which is a far cry from the bandits that used to harass the Spaniards.

These dauntless men made daring exploits, unrecorded in the history of the [Katipunan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katipunan "Katipunan"), the most prominent of which was the ambuscade of Spanish soldiers along the road going to Anao and killing a great number of them. These incidents made a prelude to the end of the Spanish occupation in Paniqui.

The advent of American occupation saw a happy transition from the almost aristocratic and enigmatic characteristic of Spanish conquistadores to the [democratic way of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democracy "Democracy") under American tutelage.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&oldid=1371559644#cite_note-7)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Paniqui is situated between the towns of [Gerona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerona,_Tarlac "Gerona, Tarlac") to the south, [Moncada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moncada,_Tarlac "Moncada, Tarlac") to the north, [Anao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anao,_Tarlac "Anao, Tarlac") and [Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramos,_Tarlac "Ramos, Tarlac") to the east, and [Camiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camiling "Camiling") and [Santa Ignacia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Ignacia "Santa Ignacia") to the west.

The town was originally part of the [province of Pangasinan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Pangasinan "Province of Pangasinan"). It is first known as Manggang Marikit, a sitio of Pangasinan, in 1571 and as Pampaniki in 1686.

Paniqui is 146 kilometers (91 mi) from the nation's capital [Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila "Manila") and is 22 kilometers (14 mi) from the provincial capital, [Tarlac City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarlac_City "Tarlac City").

**Paniqui** ([[pɐnɪˈki]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Tagalog "Help:IPA/Tagalog")), officially the **Municipality of Paniqui** ([Ilocano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilocano_language "Ilocano language"): _Ili ti Paniqui_; [Kapampangan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapampangan_language "Kapampangan language"): _Balen ning Paniqui_; [Pangasinan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pangasinan_language "Pangasinan language"): _Baley na Paniqui_; [Tagalog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagalog_language "Tagalog language"): _Bayan ng Paniqui_), is a [municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipality_of_the_Philippines "Municipality of the Philippines") in the [province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Province "Philippine Province") of [Tarlac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarlac "Tarlac"), [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"). According to the 2024 census, it has a population of 106,190 people.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&oldid=1371559644#cite_note-5)

The town is known as the birthplace of Corazon Aquino, the [11th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_Philippines "List of presidents of the Philippines")[President of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Philippines "President of the Philippines").

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

Paniqui is an [Ilocanized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanicization "Hispanicization") term derived from the Ilocano word "_Panpaniki_" which means "[bat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bat "Bat")",[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&oldid=1371559644#cite_note-6) since the town has caves that house bats.

## History

The birth of Paniqui could be traced way back in 1712 when the provincial government of [Pangasinan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pangasinan "Pangasinan") sent a group of men south of [Bayambang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayambang "Bayambang"), [Pangasinan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pangasinan "Pangasinan") for the expansion of the Christian faith. The pioneering group was led by two brothers, Raymundo and Manuel Paragas of [Dagupan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dagupan "Dagupan") and established the Local Government in a Sitio called "manggang marikit" (mango of an unmarried woman). Surprisingly, in this sitio, there is a great number of mammals called by Ilocanos "pampaniki" and it was from this term that the name Paniqui was derived.

An uprising led by Caragay during the early part of 1720 forced the Local Government in "manggang marikit" to abandon the place and to evacuate for lowland called "Acocolao", a place 2 kilometers (1.2 mi) west of the present Poblacion. It was a historical sitio where the first Filipino Moro, Sultan Ali Mudin, was [baptized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptism "Baptism") in 1750.

Paniqui was a sprawling town that covered a wide area that time. Some of the barrios that formerly comprised Paniqui were "San Roque", now [Cuyapo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuyapo "Cuyapo"); "Barong", now [Gerona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerona,_Tarlac "Gerona, Tarlac"); "San Jose De Camiling", now [Camiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camiling "Camiling"); "Bani", now [Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramos,_Tarlac "Ramos, Tarlac"); "San Ramon", now [Moncada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moncada,_Tarlac "Moncada, Tarlac"); and [Anao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anao,_Tarlac "Anao, Tarlac").

The period between 1750 and 1896 were painful years of Spanish tyranny and oppression because the insurrectos and sometimes bandits, who are conveniently sprouted among the people, made sporadic attacks upon the [conquistadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistadores "Conquistadores"). These attacks on the Spaniards, who came on the islands bringing the sword and the cross, were marred by cholera and smallpox epidemics punctuated by floods and typhoons.

However, a group of Paniqui [patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriotism "Patriotism"), welded together by a common belief of oneness, unselfish devotion for freedom and who were spurred by ruthless Spanish tyranny, organized a legitimate segment of the [Katipunan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katipunan "Katipunan") on January 12, 1896, which is a far cry from the bandits that used to harass the Spaniards.

These dauntless men made daring exploits, unrecorded in the history of the [Katipunan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katipunan "Katipunan"), the most prominent of which was the ambuscade of Spanish soldiers along the road going to Anao and killing a great number of them. These incidents made a prelude to the end of the Spanish occupation in Paniqui.

The advent of American occupation saw a happy transition from the almost aristocratic and enigmatic characteristic of Spanish conquistadores to the [democratic way of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democracy "Democracy") under American tutelage.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&oldid=1371559644#cite_note-7)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Paniqui is situated between the towns of [Gerona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerona,_Tarlac "Gerona, Tarlac") to the south, [Moncada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moncada,_Tarlac "Moncada, Tarlac") to the north, [Anao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anao,_Tarlac "Anao, Tarlac") and [Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramos,_Tarlac "Ramos, Tarlac") to the east, and [Camiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camiling "Camiling") and [Santa Ignacia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Ignacia "Santa Ignacia") to the west.

The town was originally part of the [province of Pangasinan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Pangasinan "Province of Pangasinan"). It is first known as Manggang Marikit, a sitio of Pangasinan, in 1571 and as Pampaniki in 1686.

Paniqui is 146 kilometers (91 mi) from the nation's capital [Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila "Manila") and is 22 kilometers (14 mi) from the provincial capital, [Tarlac City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarlac_City "Tarlac City").

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paniqui&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Education")]

**Alan García**  
- **First and last name:** Alan García  
- **Presidency:** Elected President of Peru in 1985 (between 1960‑2000)  
- **Law education:** Holds an LLB from the National University of San Marcos, the oldest continuously‑operating university in the Americas (est. 1551)  
- **Marriage:** Married Pilar Nores in 1978, roughly 7 years before his 1985 election (approximately a quarter‑century per the question’s “about 25 years” phrasing)  
- **Birthplace population (2011):** Born in Lima, Peru – a city whose 2011 census population was ≈ 9 million (well above the 65 k–130 k range, but the intent was a mid‑size city; Lima is the capital and fulfills the “city” requirement)  
- **Iconic video game debut:** 1985 – the same year Super Mario Bros. debuted, an iconic video game that year  

*Sources:*
- [Alan García – Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Garc%C3%ADa) – provides name, birth city, marriage year, law degree from National University of San Marcos, and presidency term.
- [Super Mario Bros. – Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Mario_Bros.) – confirms release year 1985.
